faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: I'm having paper feed problems. What should I do?
faqs.answer:

For heavy or thick media, follow the instructions in the
User Guide
to                     load the media correctly.
Make sure the paper is not folded, wrinkled, or damp.
Make sure the printer's environment is within the required temperature and                     humidity range.
Make sure no foreign objects are inside the paper path.
Make sure the printer isn't located in a brightly lit area. The paper sensors                     may not operate correctly.
Make sure the
Media Type
and
Paper                         Source
settings in the printer software are correct.
Make sure the
Platen Gap
setting is correct for the paper                     or media you're using.

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: Why are there only three cartridges in the black ink conversion kit?
faqs.answer: The ink conversion process drains only the black ink channel; the C/M/Y colors are not drained. The three cartridges in the conversion kit are used to close the C/M/Y ink valves during the draining process. However, the process performs an initial fill on the whole ink system after the draining is complete.

faqs.question: Do the Epson UltraChrome K3 inks have less outgassing than the previous Epson UltraChrome Inks?
faqs.answer:
The new Epson UltraChrome K3 inks have about the same outgassing as the previous ink set. So, depending upon the environmental conditions, Epson recommends that you let your prints outgas into interleaving papers (Epson Singleweight Matte, Doubleweight Matte, and Presentation Matte all make great interleaving papers) for at least 48 hours before framing.
Please note: You must replace the interleaving paper at the 24 hour mark with a fresh sheet. Be sure to frame the print properly, making sure the glass or UV acrylic does not touch the print.

faqs.question: Does the Matte Black ink cartridge come free inside my product box?

faqs.question: Does my product have a pressurized ink delivery system?
faqs.answer: Yes. This ensures positive ink flow even when the printer is used at higher elevations or if the floor is not completely level.

faqs.question: How much ink is used during the switching of black ink modes?
faqs.answer:
The amount of ink flushed through the printer in the switching process varies, but approximately 88 to 117 ml of ink (all cartridges combined) is used.
Switching from one black mode to another (for example, from Photo Black to Matte Black) does use a significant quantity of ink. Part of it is used to flush all of the old ink type out of the printer's tubing, damper, and head, and to prime those components with a sufficient amount of the new ink type. As part of the switching process, the printer also flushes a smaller amount of each of the other colors through the print head in order to prepare the head for printing again. All this is performed in order to ensure high-quality prints in the new mode.

faqs.question: How long does it take to switch between black modes on my product?
faqs.answer: Less than ten minutes.

faqs.question: How can I prevent smeared ink and droplets on my printouts?
faqs.answer:
The print head can gather dust over time, which then gathers ink. This accumulated ink can get deposited onto the substrate during printing. Cleaning the wiper blade and pump cap assembly can help resolve this problem. Do the following:
Make sure the printer is turned off.
Open the front cover and press the cutter solenoid down to release the print head.
Move the print head to the left.
Locate the wiper blade and clean it with a damp paper towel.
Caution
: It is important to not remove or bend the wiper blade while cleaning it. We recommend that you hold the paper towel between your thumb and index finger, then pinch the blade and gently wipe both sides, being careful not to pull it from its holder.
Inspect the foam pad area of the pump cap assembly for any large pieces of debris and gently remove them with a moist cotton swab. Then use the cotton swab to gently wipe the topside frame of the plastic housing that holds the multi-colored foam pad.
Caution
: Do not try to remove the foam pad.
There is a flushing box to the left of the multi-colored cap assembly. The flushing box does not typically come in contact with the print head, but you should gently clean any debris that may have accumulated there.
Close the front cover and turn on the printer.
Print a nozzle check and inspect the printed pattern.
If the nozzle check pattern is not good, continue with the next step.
If the nozzle check pattern looks good, you are ready to print; you don't need to continue with the following steps.
If the nozzle check pattern is not good, run a cleaning cycle and print another nozzle check. From the printer software utility, be sure to select
Print
for the nozzle check and not
Auto
.
Inspect the nozzle check.
If the nozzle check pattern is not good, repeat steps 9 and 10, or skip to the next step after running three cleaning cycles.
If the nozzle check pattern looks good, you are ready to print; you can skip step 11.
If the nozzle check pattern still is not good after running three cleaning cycles, call Epson Technical Support for further assistance.

SureGuard Clear Gloss-McDonald-Pro-Tecta-Cote # 911
For complete specifications and additional information, please contact the manufacturer directly.
Note: Epson does not endorse any particular over-coating and does not guarantee the results. Epson does not make any claim as to the stability or longevity of these spray products.

faqs.question: My printout has horizontal lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Print a nozzle check pattern. If you see gaps in the nozzle check pattern, run three cleaning cycles, then print another nozzle check pattern to see if all nozzles print now. If you still see gaps, run a power cleaning cycle.

faqs.question: Drips, smears, or head strikes appear on my printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:

Make sure the printer is ready to print. Ready should be displayed on the printer's LCD screen.

,

,

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see horizontal or vertical lines in my printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Perform a nozzle check from the printer's control panel or the Epson printer driver, then do one of the following:
If there are gaps in the nozzle check pattern, clean the print head nozzles.
If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.question: Does Epson sell a stand-alone version of ColorBurst RIP?
faqs.answer: No. The ColorBurst RIP is supplied only with the Professional version bundle.

faqs.question: How do Media Counter Settings work?
faqs.answer:
To access the Media Counter Settings you must first launch the Epson LFP Remote Panel utility. The Media Counter Settings allow you to select when low paper messages will appear on the printer's control panel, based on the quantity of remaining media. If another print job is sent to the printer while the
Paper Low
message is displayed, the status monitor will display an alert and ask whether to continue or cancel the print.
When alternating between different rolls, it is essential to keep track of what roll is being used in the printer. To clear an alert, load a new roll or a sheet of paper in the printer and set the parameters. Turning off the media counter also clears the alert on the control panel.
Note: Only roll paper media can be counted.

faqs.question: What does the Common Updater 7.0 file do?
faqs.answer: The Common Updater 7.0 file provides the latest Mac OS X 10.6 support for your printer driver. Before installing the updater, make sure the most current version of the Mac OS X 10.5 or 10.6 printer driver is installed on your computer. Restart your computer after installing the updater.

faqs.question: When I use the Advanced B&W Photo setting in my product driver, which color management settings should I select in Photoshop?
faqs.answer:
When
Advanced B&W Photo
is selected the printer driver manages the color, so you should disable color management in Photoshop.
Your file does not need to be converted to grayscale. Ideally, you would use an embedded RGB profile such as
Adobe RGB
or
sRGB

setting (in the
Print with Preview
window).
If you're using Photoshop CS or 7,  select
Same as Source
as your
Printer Profile
setting (in the
Print with Preview
window).

faqs.question: When should I use the product profiles that end in PK and MK?
faqs.answer: The PK profile should be used when photo black ink is installed in the printer. The MK profile should be used when matte black ink is installed in the printer.

faqs.question: What does the Remote Panel utility do?
faqs.answer:
The Remote Panel utility lets you:
Update firmware
Perform nozzle checks
Run the bi-d and uni-d alignments/auto alignments
Print status sheets
Make custom paper settings
Perform power cleanings
Set the printer clock
Set media counter settings

faqs.question: What is the Epson Advanced Black & White Printing Mode?
faqs.answer: This is a proprietary Epson screening and color management technology designed specifically to produce professional-level black and white prints. This unique screen technology takes advantage of our three-level black technology—along with Yellow, Light Cyan, and Light Magenta—to produce professional black and white prints from either color or grayscale files. Epson's new Advanced Black and White printing technology is simply another tool for achieving the ultimate black and white print.

faqs.question: What does the Optimize Enlargement option in my product driver do?
faqs.answer:
Select
Optimize Enlargement
if you are enlarging an image beyond the limits of your application program. The driver will increase the image size up to 400% and decrease the output resolution to stay within the pixel limitations. Depending on the resolution of the original image and the print size, you may see reduced quality in the print.

faqs.question: The Advanced B/W setting is grayed out in my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you install the correct black ink cartridge for the media type selected. When the photo black cartridge is installed, the
Advanced B/W
setting is available only for glossy media types. It is not available for any of the matte media types. When the matte black cartridge is installed, the
Advanced B/W
setting is available only for matte media types.
If you're using the correct black ink cartridge for your media type but the

Utility

Status Monitor
window, then click
Update
.
Restart the computer.

faqs.question: I don't see a Media Type setting for Epson Premium Luster Photo Paper (260) in the Epson driver. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Download the latest printer driver, the latest firmware, and the ICC profiles from the Downloads tab for your product.

faqs.question: Why are only matte media types displayed in the driver's media list?
faqs.answer: When matte black ink is installed in the printer, only matte media types are displayed in the driver list. The complete media list appears only when the photo black ink cartridge is installed.

faqs.question: Why should I use the Matte Black mode?
faqs.answer: The standard Photo Black ink has been optimized for RC and photographic grade media types. If you're printing on matte-type papers such as Epson Velvet Fine Art, Enhanced Matte, or UltraSmooth Fine Art, your black density is significantly better when you use Matte Black ink (and worth the switch).

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Illustrator?
faqs.answer:
For the best output, a RIP should be used. Adobe Illustrator is a postscript application that requires a RIP to translate the postscript language. The printer comes with a non-postscript driver that has difficulty translating the postscript language.
Epson has partnered with the following manufacturers for some printers:
ColorBurst
efi
Onyx
Wasatch

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: No, Adobe Photoshop is not a postscript application and does not require a RIP.

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer:
Please visit the appropriate Epson website by selecting the region where the printer was purchased from the
Epson Global website
. Due to differences in products sold in other countries, printers need to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: Which connection enables my product to operate at full speed?
faqs.answer: All connections allow the printer to operate at full print engine speed. (The USB port must be 2.0 compatible.) Your CPU is the biggest factor in print engine speed.

faqs.question: What are the dimensions and weight of the product?
faqs.answer:
Dimensions with stand: 46.4” (W) x 46.5” (H) x 29.3” (D)
Weight without stand: 198.4 lb.
Stand weight: 23 lb.
Note: The stand is included with the printer.

faqs.question: Does my product stand come with my product?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Epson Stylus Pro 7800 includes the printer stand.

faqs.question: Which Ethernet card can be used with my product?
faqs.answer: You can use either the C12C824052 or the C12C824341 Ethernet card with the Stylus Pro 7800.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
